title: The Colossus: Popular Picture and Likely Truth
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Hover over and click six scenes, the popular picture of the Colossus of Rhodes on the left and what the evidence supports on the right, for its pose, its place, and its end, then test yourself in Quiz mode.

educational.topic: The Colossus of Rhodes: myth and evidence
learningObjectives: The learner will separate what most people imagine about the Colossus of Rhodes from what the book's evidence supports, and apply the *myth versus history* test from Chapter 4 to three parts of the story: the pose, the place, and the end.
prerequisites: Myth versus history, from [Chapter 4](../../chapters/04-byzantine-constantinople/index.md), and the Colossus, from [Chapter 12](../../chapters/12-rhodes/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison followed by retrieval practice
keyQuestions: What is the earliest source, and how long after the event?
Which part of the popular picture lacks evidence?
commonMisconceptions: The Colossus straddled the harbor entrance.
The Colossus was carried off by camels.
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz mode: click the zone that matches each idea

controls.name: Explore
controls.description: Default mode: hover a zone for a tooltip, click it for the infobox.

controls.name: Quiz Mode
controls.description: Hides the name pills and asks 9 questions answered by clicking a zone.
